title: DX Initiative — Cohort Acceleration Hub for SDKs, Docs & Quickstarts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a repeatable, low-friction ‘Cohort Acceleration Hub’ that combines SDK onboarding flows, documentation quickstarts, and cohort-based experiments to lift new developer activation and 30-day retention. This ticket defines the playbook, success metrics, experiment harness, and an MVP orchestration plan for the next two cycles. The scope includes: (1) a cohort creation template (segmentation + automated emails/in-app prompts), (2) a canonical quickstart matrix across SDK languages, (3) an evaluation harness to measure activation/retention signals and quality regressions, and (4) rollout automation hooks for Growth and Solutions teams.
acceptance_criteria: Cohort template implemented and documented (segmentation rules, cadence, messaging) and accessible to Growth via Console
Three SDK quickstarts (JS, Python, Go) published in docs with runnable examples and CI-verified tests
Evaluation harness wired to metrics dashboard (activation funnel, 7d and 30d retention, error rates) and baseline established
At least two pilot cohorts executed with instrumented signals and a post-cohort retrospective summarizing learnings
Playbook published in Confluence with step-by-step rollout checklist and escalation paths
milestones: 2026-01-30: Quickstart authoring complete for JS/Python; Go quickstart skeletoned
2026-02-08: Instrumentation plan landed (events, dashboards, and alerting)
2026-03-15: Final playbook + handoff to Growth & Solutions
okrs: OKR-1: Increase new SDK user 7-day activation rate from 18% to 30% for cohorted users by end of Q1
OKR-2: Improve 30-day retention for cohort participants by +12 percentage points versus baseline
OKR-3: Reduce time-to-first-successful-inference (TTFSI) in quickstarts from median 22 minutes to <=10 minutes
metrics: Activation funnel: signup -> first API call -> first successful response (target conversion 30%)
30-day retention delta (cohort vs non-cohort), baseline comparison weekly
Quickstart run rate: percent of users who complete quickstart within 24 hours of signup (target 25%)

risks: Risk: Quickstart fragility across customer network environments could increase support load. Mitigation: add robust retry guidance and CI tests that simulate throttle/errors.
Risk: Instrumentation gaps (missing event or inconsistent properties) will make cohort analysis noisy. Mitigation: enforce schema and automated validation in CI.
Risk: Dependencies on Dedicated routing work could delay rollout to enterprise cohorts. Mitigation: run public-cloud cohorts first and prepare an enterprise-specific runbook.
